title: Sales Tax Base on a Total Loss: Lienholder and Lessor Vehicles
content:
**Rule.** Under the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), the tax base of the owner's tax-and-title payment depends on the kind of loss payee listed on the coverage:
- **Lessor.** When the loss payee is a lessor, there is no tax base, since the lessor holds the title and the tax on a lease.
- **Lienholder, value recognised below the declared value.** When the loss payee is a lienholder and the vehicle value recognised is less than the actual cash value on the total loss declaration, the tax base is the declared actual cash value.
- **Otherwise.** The tax base is the vehicle value recognised.

**The vehicle value recognised** is the total loss payment made to the loss payee on the claim, plus the deductible that payment carries.

### Hypothetical cases

| Loss payee kind | Value recognised (USD) | Declared actual cash value (USD) | Tax base (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lessor | 14,200.00 | 14,900.00 | None |
| Lienholder | 10,850.00 | 11,300.00 | 11,300.00 |
| Lienholder | 11,300.00 | 11,300.00 | 11,300.00 |
| Lienholder | 11,640.00 | 11,300.00 | 11,640.00 |

The last two rows show the boundary. A value recognised equal to or above the declared actual cash value is itself the base.
